regression_fixed_during_this_phase: tracker.upsert_job() and search_worker._upsert_job_identity_only() initially made the 3 new discovery_* columns unconditional, which broke scripts/test_registry_pipeline.py (a legacy test using an un-migrated schema). Fixed by making both functions detect column presence via PRAGMA table_info(jobs) at call time and building their INSERT column list dynamically -- a database that predates this migration keeps working exactly as before. Full suite re-verified clean after the fix.
architectural_notes: Search-provider adapters are registered under NEW keys (LINKEDIN_SEARCH, INDEED_SEARCH, ...), deliberately distinct from the pre-existing LINKEDIN/INDEED/... Phase 4 direct-crawl skeletons (still NOT_ENABLED, reserved for a hypothetical future authorized direct API). Every job record these new adapters emit still carries source='LINKEDIN' (the real board), so job_id.py's URL-derived identity means a manually-imported or future-directly-discovered job for the same URL naturally dedupes against a search-provider-discovered one.

AdapterStatus for all seven search-provider adapters is fixed once at class-definition/first-import time from search_provider.is_serper_configured() -- the same convention every other adapter in this codebase already uses (a plain class attribute, not re-evaluated per call). This is why _default_sources()/discover_from_sources() automatically include or exclude these sources exactly as they do for every other source, with zero changes to search_profile.py, query_planner.py, or search_worker.py.

The Claude/agent WebSearch capability (used in Phase 13 purely as one-off evidence capture) is explicitly NOT the production backend here -- SerperProvider talks to Serper.dev's own HTTP API via urllib, independently of any agent session.

Hostname validation was hardened relative to the uploaded reference implementation, which used a substring check (`domain not in netloc`) vulnerable to a lookalike host like 'notlinkedin.com.evil.example'. restricted_source_registry.is_safe_url() instead requires an exact host match or a genuine dot-separated subdomain.
